From 57560ee95cb7f91cf0bc31d4ae8276e0dcfe17aa Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Martin Kepplinger <martin.kepplinger@puri.sm>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2021 08:18:07 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] usb: typec: tipd: Don't block probing of consumer of
 "connector" nodes

Similar as with tcpm this patch lets fw_devlink know not to wait on the
fwnode to be populated as a struct device.

Without this patch, USB functionality can be broken on some previously
supported boards.

Fixes: 28ec344bb891 ("usb: typec: tcpm: Don't block probing of consumers of "connector" nodes")
Cc: stable <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Acked-by: Heikki Krogerus <heikki.krogerus@linux.intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Martin Kepplinger <martin.kepplinger@puri.sm>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20210714061807.5737-1-martin.kepplinger@puri.sm
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

diff --git a/drivers/usb/typec/tipd/core.c b/drivers/usb/typec/tipd/core.c
index 938219bc1b4b..21b3ae25c76d 100644
--- a/drivers/usb/typec/tipd/core.c
+++ b/drivers/usb/typec/tipd/core.c
@@ -629,6 +629,15 @@ static int tps6598x_probe(struct i2c_client *client)
 	if (!fwnode)
 		return -ENODEV;
 
+	/*
+	 * This fwnode has a "compatible" property, but is never populated as a
+	 * struct device. Instead we simply parse it to read the properties.
+	 * This breaks fw_devlink=on. To maintain backward compatibility
+	 * with existing DT files, we work around this by deleting any
+	 * fwnode_links to/from this fwnode.
+	 */
+	fw_devlink_purge_absent_suppliers(fwnode);
+
 	tps->role_sw = fwnode_usb_role_switch_get(fwnode);
 	if (IS_ERR(tps->role_sw)) {
 		ret = PTR_ERR(tps->role_sw);
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/usb/typec/tipd/core.c`**
   - A new block of code has been added to the `tps6598x_probe` function. This block includes a comment explaining the purpose of the modification and a call to `fw_devlink_purge_absent_suppliers(fwnode);`.
   - This addition ensures that the firmware device link does not block the probing of consumers of "connector" nodes by purging any fwnode links associated with the fwnode that is not populated as a struct device.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification in `core.c` directly addresses an issue related to the firmware device link (fw_devlink) mechanism. By purging absent suppliers, the patch prevents the blocking of USB functionality on certain boards that rely on the "connector" nodes. This change is similar to a previous fix made for the `tcpm` driver, indicating a broader issue with how device links are managed in the USB Type-C subsystem. The patch aims to maintain backward compatibility with existing device tree files while ensuring that the system can function correctly without unnecessary delays in device probing.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
fwnode = device_get_named_child_node(&client->dev, "connector");
if (!fwnode)
    return -ENODEV;
```
Reason:
The bug occurs because the `fwnode` representing the "connector" node is not populated as a struct device. The firmware device link (fw_devlink) mechanism incorrectly blocks the probing of consumers of this node, leading to broken USB functionality as the system waits indefinitely for a device that will never be created.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
fw_devlink_purge_absent_suppliers(fwnode);
```
Reason:
This statement removes any firmware device links associated with the `fwnode` that are not populated as a struct device. By purging these absent suppliers, the patch allows the probing of consumers to proceed without being blocked, thus restoring USB functionality on affected boards.
